cells.quote: For AC afferents, 85% (50/59) of LA interneurons received input (Fig. 3a), and the evoked EPSC had a peak amplitude of 167 ± 25 pA. ... AC input to BA interneurons was also sparse with 38% of cells (6/16; Fig. 3b) being innervated, but input to individual cells (127 ± 50 pA) was not signiﬁcantly different to that in the LA ( p = 0.5888).
cells.note: The contrast is positive for innervation prevalence, while evoked amplitude did not significantly differ.

O.outcome_detail: AMPAR rectification index and calcium-permeable AMPAR expression

result.effect: BA rectification index 0.35 ± 0.04 (n = 45) vs LA 0.25 ± 0.02 (n = 54), p < 0.05

cells.quote: The AMPAR rectiﬁcation index was measured as the ratio of peak AMPAR EPSC amplitude at +40 mV and −60 mV in the presence of NMDAR blocker d-AP5 (30 μM), and was signiﬁcantly higher in BA interneurons (BA: 0.35 ± 0.04, n = 45; LA: 0.25 ± 0.02, n = 54; p < 0.05; Fig. 5a, c; Supplementary Fig. 2b), suggesting that glutamatergic synapses on BA interneurons contained fewer GluR2-lacking, calcium permeable (CP)-AMPA receptors.
cells.note: Higher BA rectification was interpreted as fewer calcium-permeable AMPA receptors in BA synapses.

result.effect: LA normalized EPSC amplitude 1.5 ± 0.1 (n = 9); BA n = 8, LTP not induced

cells.quote: All interneurons in the BA express synaptic NMDA receptors (Fig. 5h), however, tetanic stimulation of cortical input to interneurons in the BA failed to evoke LTP ( n = 8; Fig. 6 a, b). In contrast, as reported previously 38, tetanic stimulation of cortical inputs onto LA interneurons expressing GluN2A-containing NMDA receptors reliably evoked LTP (normalized EPSC amplitude = 1.5 ± 0.1; n = 9; Fig. 6c, d).
cells.note: This is a physiological plasticity contrast between amygdala nuclei, not an educational learning outcome.
